To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
biennial mammography screening is associated with a larger tumor size among premenopausal obese women, but not with higher stage or larger tumor size among postmenopausal obese or overweight women.

biennial mammography screening does not appear to adversely impact stage of diagnosis or tumor size in postmenopausal obese women, and that biennial screening may be associated with a larger tumor size in premenopausal obese patients.

the only negative outcome for biennial screening was a larger breast cancer size in obese premenopausals, and since annual mammography does no improve stage at diagnosis and has higher false positive rates, women and their providers should weigh the risks and benefits when choosing between annual and biennial screening.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the mammography screening interval on breast cancer diagnosis.
the impact of the screening mammography interval on the detection of breast cancer and false positive recall/biopsy.
the impact of screening mammography interval on breast cancer diagnosis by menopausal and BMI status.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
biennial screening may be a reasonable option for women with average risk of breast cancer.
the harms of biennial vs. yearly screening may be less than the harms of yearly screening.
the evidence is insufficient to determine whether biennial or annual mammography screening is better.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
biennial screening is a reasonable option for women aged 40-74, regardless of menopausal status or BMI.
the harms of annual screening are higher than the benefits, especially for obese women.
biennial screening is as effective as annual screening and is better for women in terms of false positive recalls and biopsies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
biennial screening is a safe alternative to annual mammography.
women with breast cancer do not have worse outcomes if they are screened biennially rather than annually.
the benefits of annual screening are not as great for women with higher BMI as for women with lower BMI, and the harms of annual screening are greater for women with lower BMIs.
